title: Soft Lithographic Functionalization and Patterning Oxide-free Silicon and Germanium
protocol: Cut silicon wafer into 1cm² substrates.
Dust and rinse silicon substrates with water and filtered ethanol.
Submerge the silicon substrates in Nano strip at 75°C for 15 minutes.
Rinse each substrate with deionized, filtered water.
Place each substrate in a 5% HF solution for 5 minutes.
Dry oxide-free silicon with nitrogen.
Immerse each oxide-free silicon piece in a saturated PCl5 in chlorobenzene solution and filter to 0.2 μm.
Assemble a vial condenser on top of each vial containing the silicon pieces.
Place the vials in a heatblock set to 112°C for one hour.
Rinse each surface with chlorobenzene after cooling.
Dry under filtered nitrogen.
Place each chlorinated silicon surface in propenyl magnesium chloride solution at 130 °C for 24 hours.
Cool the pressure vial containing propenyl-terminated substrate and rinse with DCM and ethanol.
Dry under filtered nitrogen.
Cut germanium wafer into 1cm² substrates.
Dust and rinse germanium substrates with water and filtered ethanol.
Submerge surfaces in acetone for 20 minutes to remove organic contamination.
Place each surface in a 10% HCl solution for 15 minutes to chlorinate the surface.
Dry the substrates with nitrogen after 5 minutes.
Place each chlorinated germanium surface in a pressure vial containing 4 ml of octyl magnesium chloride (2 mM).
Heat the pressure vials at 130 °C for 48 hours.
Let cooled pressure vials reach room temperature before opening.
Rinse each surface quickly with DCM and ethanol.
Dry under filtered nitrogen after rinsing.
Prepare a filtered 0.1 M NHS-diazirine solution in carbon tetrachloride.
Pipette a few drops of the solution onto methyl terminated surfaces.
Place the surfaces under a UV lamp (☐=254 nm, 4400/cm² at 0.74 inches) for 30 minutes.
Add more NHS-diazirine to the surface and let react for an additional 30 minutes.
Rinse NHS modified surfaces with DCM and ethanol.
Dry under filtered nitrogen after rinsing.
React NHS-modified substrates in a 20 mM tert-butyl carbamoyl (Boc-) ethylenediamine solution in dichloromethane (DCM) for two hours at room temperature.
Rinse the Boc-modified substrate with DCM and ethanol.
Deprotect the Boc modified substrate using 25% trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) in DCM for one hour at room temperature.
Rinse the resulting surface with DCM, ethanol, and 10% (w/v) potassium bicarbonate in water.
Dry under filtered nitrogen.
Analyze all surfaces by XPS to determine the elemental composition.
Dilute acrylate A by 30% with trimethylolpropane ethoxylate triacrylate B.
Add photoinitiators C and D to the reaction mixture.
Add sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate (0.2 g, 1.22 mmol) to a 4N HCl solution in dioxane (10 ml).
Stir at room temperature for 2 minutes.
Filter off the sodium chloride first through a fine glass filter and then through a 0.2 μm PTFE membrane syringe filter.
Evaporate dioxane under reduced pressure.
React the resulting sulfonic acid with 2 ml of the polyurethane-acrylate prepolymeric mixture at room temperature.
Then react under vacuum at 50 °C to free the mixture from trapped air bubbles.
Cool the resulting solution to room temperature and polymerize between two glass microscope slides or a glass slide and a master by exposure to UV light for 2 hours at room temperature.
Peel the stamp off the master after polymerization.
Wash the stamp with ethanol and water.
Dry the stamp with filtered nitrogen.
Place the polyurethane-acrylate stamp on the NHS-modified substrate at room temperature for one minute.
Separate the stamp and substrate after reaction.
Rinse the substrate with ethanol, water, and ethanol.
Dry the substrate with filtered nitrogen.
Rinse the stamp with ethanol, water, and ethanol.
Dry the stamp with filtered nitrogen.
Submerge the NHS-patterned bifunctional substrate in Lysine-N,N-diacetic acid (20 mM) and Et3N (100 mM) in DMF:H2O (1:1) at room temperature for 1 hour.
Rinse the substrates with water and ethanol after incubation.
Incubate the substrates in a 50 mM NiSO4 solution for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Excessively rinse the chelated substrates with water and binding buffer (20 mM NaP, 250 mM NaCl, 10 mM imidazole, pH 7.5).
Submerge the substrates in a filtered GFP solution (~40 μM) for 1 hour at 0°C.
Rinse the substrates with binding buffer after incubation.
Rinse the substrates with PBS (pH 7.4).
Keep the substrates hydrated in PBS at 0°C until ready for fluorescence microscopy analysis.
Submerge the NHS-patterned bifunctional substrate in Lysine-N,N-diacetic acid (20 mM) and Et3N (100 mM) in DMF:H2O (1:1) at room temperature for 1 hour.
Rinse the substrate with water and ethanol.
Incubate the substrate in a 50 mM NiSO4 solution for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse the chelated substrate extensively with water and binding buffer (20 mM NaP, 250 mM NaCl, 10 mM imidazole, pH 7.5).
Submerge the substrate in a filtered GFP solution (~40 μM) for 1 hour at 0°C.
Rinse the substrate with binding buffer followed by PBS (pH 7.4).
Hydrate the substrates in PBS at 0°C until ready for fluorescence microscopy analysis.
Affix nitrilotriacetic acid-terminated (NTA) heterobifunctional linkers to the NHS-functionalized regions.
Use the NTA-patterned surface as a template for the selective attachment of hexa-histidine-tagged GFP.
